Microsoft just went down. And this was much bigger than a few people missing their emails.
Within about an hour, people in seventy-four countries were reporting problems, according to Downdetector data reported by Reuters.
Outlook mailboxes wouldn't open. Teams and Copilot were disrupted too.
Then it spread beyond the office. Government agencies in Australia and Japan were hit.
Airlines in India had trouble emailing their customers.
And in Taiwan, one financial firm reportedly went back to confirming trades... by fax. In twenty twenty-six.
So, was it a hack? Microsoft says there's no sign of malicious activity.
Instead, servers unexpectedly dropped offline. The rest took on the extra traffic. And some servers that engineers restarted stopped responding again.
No hacker. No giant surge. Just a failure inside one company's machines.
So here's the real question. If one company goes offline, why does so much of the world go with it?
Should we depend this much on one company? Tell me in the comments.
